A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same Blink research work. All 16 pages, including equations, figures, tables, and Appendices A–H, are readable and support a complete comparison.

before.justification: v2 reports original benchmark evaluations, ablations, and attention analyses in Section 4 and the appendices, including experiments on three model backbones.

after.justification: v3 retains those original benchmark results, ablations, and attention analyses, including Tables 1–3 and 5–9.

M1.justification: The saliency-guided scanning, TokenSR architecture and training objective, token expansion/drop procedures, and Algorithm 1 are unchanged.

E1.justification: Both versions use the same training mixture and evaluate MME, GQA, MMBench, MMBench-CN, POPE, ScienceQA, and MM-Vet. The appendices introduce no coverage differences.

E2.justification: Comparator membership is unchanged: Tables 1, 5, and 6 retain the vanilla backbone and Blink-interp comparisons, and Table 7 retains ViCrop.

E3.justification: The backbones, metrics, training configuration, preprocessing, layer ranges, saliency thresholds, and ablation settings match across both versions.

E4.justification: The module, threshold, layer-range, patch-number, and interpolation ablations are retained unchanged, as are the attention redistribution analyses in Section 4 and Appendices E–G.

E5.justification: Both versions report the same point results without repeated-run counts, seed information, confidence intervals, or significance tests. No uncertainty-reporting practice changes.

E6.justification: Numerical entries and plotted findings are unchanged throughout the main text and appendices. For example, Blink's Table 1 MME perception and cognition totals remain 1519.74 and 361.79.

T1.justification: The mathematical definitions and Equations 1–6 are unchanged, as are the patch-adjusted threshold formulas in Appendix F. No assumptions, derivations, or proofs are added or revised.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, contribution statements, and conclusion retain the same claims about attention behavior and dynamic visual-token enhancement within a single forward pass.

C2.justification: Result interpretations and applicability qualifications are unchanged. Appendix H retains the limitations concerning convolution-based upsampling and unverified scalability beyond 7B models.

D1.justification: v3 adds a footnote in Appendix A.1 stating that code is available and linking to the Blink repository. v2 lacks this access information; the implementation and training details otherwise match.

R1.justification: The cited works, bibliography, related-work discussion, and positioning against prior visual-perception methods are unchanged.

P1.justification: v3 removes the trailing comma after the final author's name, updates the version/date stamp, and inserts the code-availability footnote. The existing prose and section order are unchanged.

P2.justification: The new footnote causes column and page reflow across appendix pages 12–15, including moving Appendix B's heading into the right column. Figures, tables, captions, and their substantive displays remain unchanged.

improvement.justification: The added code-location footnote in Appendix A.1 modestly improves implementation discoverability and reproducibility documentation. The scientific evidence and limitations are unchanged. This gain concerns the documented access information; repository contents are not established by the PDFs.
